title: Mattityahu the High Priest
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Mattityahu the High Priest. (Biblical namesake: Mattityahu, I Chronicles 25:21.) Megillah 11a expounds “I did not abhor them” as the Greek period, when God raised up Shimon HaTzaddik, Chashmonai and his sons, and Mattityahu the High Priest.

Hyman has already explained elsewhere at length that he was never High Priest: in his time the wicked Yoan was High Priest, as related in Antiquities and the books of the Hasmoneans; after him came the wicked Menelaus, and no Hasmonean High Priest was appointed until Yonatan. In Hyman’s explanation, the Sages called Mattityahu High Priest because he first called for the sword on behalf of the Lord, His people and His Torah, and saved the people from destruction. His name therefore remained a blessing as Mattityahu the High Priest.

notes.text: The denial of actual high-priestly service and explanation of an honorific title are Hyman’s historical argument. Yoan remains his name-form; it is not silently identified as Yohanan. The Chronicles figure is a Biblical namesake.

The consulted Megillah 11a explicitly names Mattityahu as High Priest; I Chronicles 25:21 supplies a Biblical namesake. Hyman’s denial that he actually held office, Yoan/Menelaus chronology and explanation of an honorific are his historical argument, not findings independently established from Antiquities or Maccabees here.
